sections.body: Legal Operations, Infrastructure and Security is the back office of AI in law, the place where models run, data sits, time is recorded, knowledge is kept, and clients arrive. AI is actually doing document intake, conflict checks, matter triage, time narrative drafting, and retrieval over firm knowledge, often through local or private deployments. Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment puts a model on firm hardware or an isolated network so client data does not leave the perimeter. Secure Storage and Networking for Legal Data covers encryption, access control, logging, and segmented networks that keep matter files separate. Timekeeping and Billing Narratives use language models to turn raw activity into descriptive entries, while Firm Knowledge Management uses search and summarization over past work product. Client Intake and Triage use AI to parse inquiries, flag urgency, and route matters, though a human still decides engagement.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is partly solved and partly fragile, because local deployment is real for open weight models but performance, hardware cost, and update cadence remain hard tradeoffs. Secure storage and networking are mature in general IT terms, yet legal data adds ethical walls, retention rules, and cross border limits that generic tools do not handle well. Billing narrative generation works for routine entries but needs review because small errors become fee disputes. Knowledge management retrieves and summarizes, but it does not guarantee that the right precedent or clause is found, and stale or inconsistent documents poison results. Client intake and triage can classify and route, but it cannot make legal judgments, and it can encode bias or miss urgency. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, while its 219 compliance and regulation pages and 6978 state AI bills show a patchwork that no single deployment can ignore.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section form a chain from infrastructure to daily operations, and they are meant to be read as connected layers rather than isolated topics. A reader goes to Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment to understand how models run on firm hardware or an isolated network, and that choice sets constraints for everything else. A reader goes to Secure Storage and Networking for Legal Data to understand encryption, access control, and network segmentation for client matter files. A reader goes to Timekeeping and Billing Narratives to see how activity data becomes descriptive billing text, which depends on the capture and storage rules above. A reader goes to Firm Knowledge Management to see how past work product is retrieved and summarized for current matters, using the same access controls. A reader goes to Client Intake and Triage to see how new inquiries are parsed and routed before they reach knowledge systems or billing.
